transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-24
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Miles Ortega (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Zenfolio Head of Security), Marcus Reed (CTO), Anjali Rao (Platform), Tom Weber (Legal)

Auto-summary:
Quick intake to map Zenfolio's security gates for a potential pilot — main asks: SOC 2 / ISO posture, SSO/SCIM integration, RBAC and audit log retention, BYOK KMS options, and data residency/egress controls. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send certifications and diagrams, schedule private-deployment technical deep dive, customer to provide workload profile and legal contact to review DPA.

Topics:
- Certifications (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001)
- SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning
- RBAC model and admin controls
- Audit logs, log retention and export formats
- Encryption-at-rest / BYOK / HSM options
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs and egress/data residency
- Contracting / DPA timelines

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Miles Ortega: Hey everyone, uh thanks for taking the time. I'm Miles from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with me is Priya our solutions engineer. Would you like to quick round robin intros?
[00:00:12] Lina Park: Lina Park, head of security at Zenfolio. We'll mostly be driving the compliance questions.
[00:00:18] Marcus Reed: Marcus, CTO, i'll be involved on infra and quotas.
[00:00:00] Anjali Rao: Anjali, platform engineer, thanks.
[00:00:30] Miles Ortega: Great thanks. Today we wanted to map your security gates and see fit for a pilot, can you say what your current concerns are around hosted inference?
[00:00:45] Lina Park: Sure. High level: we need SOC two — um type two audits — and ISO if possible. We need SSO that can do SAML and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC with least privilege, audit logs with at least 12 months retention, and key management where we can either hold keys or do BYOK. Also data residency — some PII must stay in eu-west region.
[00:01:10] Priya Shah: Thanks Lina. On the SOC two piece, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II, we can hand over the report, and we also maintain an ISO 27001 summary — i'll send both. Quick note, though, the actual hosted stack has shared tenancy vs dedicated pools — you mentioned residency, so for eu-only requirement we'd likely recommend dedicated or private.
[00:01:36] Marcus Reed: Could you unpack the difference operationally — like latency, throughput, and also if dedicated still has any cross-tenant metadata egress?
[00:01:50] Priya Shah: Yeah so dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for your tenant, isolated request queues, and we isolate data at rest in separate volumes per customer. There is still a control-plane service that is multi-tenant unless you're on Redwood Private where you can run a customer-managed control plane. In practice audit logs and tokens can be stored in tenant-specific buckets in either dedicated or private, but for legal isolation and EU-only routing Private is the cleanest path.
[00:02:22] Lina Park: And the control-plane what data does it see? For example, are prompts stored? We have strict rules around PII in inputs.
[00:02:30] Miles Ortega: Great question. For hosted API we keep short-term request traces for observability — by default we store minimal telemetry and request metadata for 30 days. We can enable a no-retention mode for enterprise customers in dedicated/private where request payloads are not persisted. We'll document exact retention fields in the report.
[00:02:52] Tom Weber: Are you able to sign a standard DPA and support data processing terms that restrict processing to specific regions? Also curious about indemnities around data breaches.
[00:03:04] Miles Ortega: Yes we have a DPA template, we'll send the DPA and we do support regional processing restrictions for Dedicated and Private. Indemnities are negotiable and often tied to enterprise contract terms — i'll flag legal to pull standard language and share.
[00:03:20] Anjali Rao: On SSO we use Okta via SAML and SCIM. Walk me through how Redwood provisions users and maps roles.
[00:03:30] Priya Shah: We support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Typical flow: SCIM creates user objects and maps them to RBAC roles in the console. Our RBAC model has roles (admin, dev, auditor) and you can map Okta groups to those roles. For private deployments we also support SCIM over a customer-managed endpoint so provisioning doesn't cross internet egress if you need tighter isolation.
[00:04:00] Marcus Reed: Is RBAC auditable? We need to show role changes and admin actions to auditors.
[00:04:07] Priya Shah: Yes, every role change, token creation, and model rollout is logged. Logs include actor, timestamp, action, and request id. We stream audit logs to your S3 or GCS bucket if you prefer — retention policy is configurable. Default retention for hosted is 90 days, but for enterprise we can set up 12+ months.
[00:04:27] Lina Park: What format are those logs in? Structured JSON? We need to ingest into Splunk.
[00:04:34] Priya Shah: Logs are structured JSON with fields for action_type, user, role, resource_id, and full request metadata — we'll attach a sample export.
[00:04:43] Miles Ortega: I'll include console screenshots and sample logs in the follow-up.
[00:04:50] Lina Park: Encryption at rest — do you support customer-managed keys with an HSM?
[00:04:56] Priya Shah: Yes. For Dedicated and Private we support BYOK via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault), and for the strictest controls Private can be configured with an HSM-backed KMS. We also support envelope encryption patterns if needed.
[00:05:17] Marcus Reed: If we do BYOK, is there any key material that leaves our control? Like do you ever cache key material in-memory on nodes outside our environment?
[00:05:28] Priya Shah: We perform streaming decryption using customer-wrapped keys; private key material never persisted on disk. In dedicated we cache minimal wrapped keys in memory of the node for a short TTL for performance, but wrapped keys are still under your control. If you need zero-exposure we can design a gateway flow in Private where the KMS is within your VPC.
[00:05:52] Anjali Rao: On the network side, do you support VPC peering or private link style connections?
[00:05:58] Priya Shah: Yes, for Private we support VPC peering and customer-managed network connections; Dedicated supports PrivateLink for egress-restricted setups. We'll include the network topology options in the diagram.
[00:06:12] Lina Park: Audit retention and tamper-evidence — can logs be append-only and do you support immutable retention buckets?
[00:06:20] Priya Shah: We support write-once buckets and can sign logs with HMAC for tamper evidence. For legal holds we can configure long-term retention in a separate immutable store.
[00:06:31] Marcus Reed: Are background models and third-party tool calls a risk? For example, do you call external APIs during preprocessing?
[00:06:40] Miles Ortega: We don't call third-party services as part of normal inference. Any external integrations are explicit and opt-in. For hosted we do use some telemetry endpoints for product metrics, but no customer payloads are sent externally unless configured.
[00:06:57] Tom Weber: On certifications — you said SOC 2 Type II. Do you have a copy of the report and what period does it cover?
[00:07:05] Miles Ortega: We have the latest SOC 2 Type II covering 2025-07 through 2026-06, and an ISO 27001 certificate for our control plane. We'll redact sensitive auditor notes but share the attestation.
[00:07:19] Lina Park: Any third-party penetration tests? We prefer annual pentests and supply chain checks.
[00:07:26] Priya Shah: Yes, we do annual third-party pen tests and publish a summary of findings and remediations; for enterprise customers we can provide the executive summary and a remediation timeline.
[00:07:38] Anjali Rao: About usage logs and debugging traces — how granular are they? We need to be able to reconstruct a request id trace through the whole pipeline for incident response.
[00:07:48] Priya Shah: Each request has a UUID and we propagate that across services. Traces include timing for tokenization, queue wait, model execution, and post-processing. We keep full traces for 30 days by default, and we'll set up a long-term retention stream to your bucket for 12 months per your requirement.
[00:08:05] Marcus Reed: Are there any limitations on exporting logs for PII redaction? Can we get pre-redacted exports?
[00:08:13] Miles Ortega: We can configure server-side redaction rules and produce PII-redacted exports. That said, for debugging sometimes raw is helpful — that can be limited to a small set of authorized auditor roles.
[00:08:26] Lina Park: For legal we need guaranteed deletion flows. If we ask for delete of customer data, what's the SLA and proof?
[00:08:34] Priya Shah: We support deletion APIs and can provide deletion certificates. We have a standard 30-day purge window for retained telemetry, but for enterprise we can arrange a shorter SLA — 7 days is possible with a private deployment and contract terms.
[00:08:50] Tom Weber: On eDiscovery and subpoenas — what's Redwood's process?
[00:08:55] Miles Ortega: We have a legal team that handles subpoenas; we notify customers for requests that relate to their data and we only provide data per the DPA and with legal review. We'll send the standard process docs.
[00:09:07] Marcus Reed: Network egress — can you guarantee there is no cross-border egress for EU-only workloads?
[00:09:15] Priya Shah: For Private we can confine everything to a regional VPC and block inter-region routing. For Dedicated we can pin capacity to a region but the control-plane acknowledgements may cross to a central plane unless you opt for Private where the control plane is customer-managed. We'll make that explicit in the diagram.
[00:09:33] Lina Park: Logging retention again — we asked 12 months, can you do 24 months if needed?
[00:09:39] Priya Shah: Yes, 24 months is possible, storage will be billed separately and we can stream to your long-term store.
[00:09:46] Miles Ortega: Quick callout on cost tradeoffs — longer retention and BYOK/HSM increase costs and sometimes latency, we'll include a unit-cost estimate based on Anjali's workload profile.
[00:09:59] Anjali Rao: We'll share sample RPS and token distribution. For pilot we want to test with 1k qps bursts and avg sequence 1k tokens to simulate real workloads — can you support that in dedicated?
[00:10:13] Priya Shah: For Dedicated with reserved pools yes, and we can provision burst capacity. For private on-prem there are more constraints but it's doable. We'll propose an initial sizing after we see the profile.
[00:10:25] Marcus Reed: Are there gating metrics or SLOs you provide?
[00:10:29] Priya Shah: We offer latency SLOs on Dedicated (p99 targets per model class) and uptime SLAs for enterprise customers. For Private it depends on the infra you provide; we can help define SLOs in the cust contract.
[00:10:41] Lina Park: Any concerns about model hallucinations and how you handle content filtering? We have PII-sensitive prompts.
[00:10:49] Miles Ortega: We provide content filters and allow customers to plug in post-processing checks. We can also integrate evaluator hooks for quality checks before responses reach production. That sits outside of core compliance but we'll discuss guardrails in the deep dive.
[00:11:04] Tom Weber: On data retention in backups — are backups encrypted and what's their retention?
[00:11:10] Priya Shah: Backups are encrypted with customer KMS where BYOK is configured; default snapshot retention is 90 days but configurable. We'll include snapshot policies in the next docs.
[00:11:22] Lina Park: Supply chain security — do you provide SBOMs for runtime components?
[00:11:28] Priya Shah: We can provide SBOM summaries for major components and dependencies and we publish CVE remediation timelines. For enterprise we can provide more detailed attestations.
[00:11:40] Anjali Rao: For private deployments, what's the onboarding time? We have strict change windows.
[00:11:46] Priya Shah: Private on-prem onboarding typically 6–8 weeks depending on infra and approvals; VPC-hosted private is faster, often 3–4 weeks. We'll map out milestones in the technical deep dive.
[00:12:00] Marcus Reed: Ok, sounds good. Any big red flags?
[00:12:04] Miles Ortega: No immediate blockers based on what you shared. Primary route: pilot on Dedicated with BYOK and 12–24 month audit log retention; if you later need stricter residency we'll plan Private.
[00:12:18] Lina Park: We will want the SOC 2 and ISO docs and a clear diagram of data flows. Also a written statement about what is and isn't stored for hosted mode.
[00:12:29] Miles Ortega: Understood. We'll send those.
[00:12:33] Tom Weber: On contracting, i'll take the DPA and initial terms, i'll loop back with Marcus on indemnities.
[00:12:40] Marcus Reed: We'll try to get the workload numbers to you by EOD Tuesday.
[00:12:45] Anjali Rao: Yep i'll drop load profiles in the shared drive.
[00:12:49] Miles Ortega: Great, last quick recap and owners — Priya will lead technical deep dive; Miles will send compliance artifacts and DPA; Anjali provides load profile; Tom will review DPA with legal. Anything else?
[00:13:05] Lina Park: Could we also get an example runbook for incident response with Redwood?
[00:13:10] Priya Shah: Yes we'll include a sample runbook and escalation matrix.
[00:13:15] Miles Ortega: Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet.
[00:13:20] Marcus Reed: Thanks.
[00:13:22] Anjali Rao: Thanks all.
[00:13:25] END OF TRANSCRIPT

Notes: transcript shows some overlaps and a few mis-transcriptions where acronyms like SOC 2 appear as 'SOC two' in speakers. Some timestamps are rough to reflect automatic transcription cadence.
